question.value: Where do the 658, 321 and 325 GHz water masers lie relative to the star VY CMa and its dust continuum, and do they match excitation model predictions?

evidence.quote: We present ALMA observations that test these predictions and, for the first time, resolve sub-mm masers, thermal lines, and continuum.
This paper makes use of ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA $\#$2011.0.00011.SV.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Spws 0.94–1.87 GHz wide, 3840 channels each; velocity resolution 0.45 km/s (321, 658 GHz), 0.9 km/s (325 GHz)

evidence.quote: Each spw was divided into 3840 channels, but as a result of Hanning smoothing in the correlator, the finest effective velocity resolution is approximately double the channel spacing
VY CMa was observed by ALMA on 2013 16–19 August using 16–20 12 m antennas.
on baselines from 0.014–2.7 km
After subtracting the continuum, the masers were imaged using beam sizes of (0.18$''$$\times$0.09$''$) and (0.088$''$$\times$0.044$''$) at 321/325 and 658 GHz.
suggesting that we recover all the flux on scales $<6$” or $<13$” at the higher or lower frequencies.
giving a total time on VY CMa at each frequency of $\sim$1.5 hr in addition to calibration observations.
observed on 2013 16–19 August

self_calibration.value: Brightest maser channel imaged as starting model; solutions applied to all channels

evidence.quote: In each SB, the brightest maser channel was identified and imaged, providing a starting model for self-calibration.
partial uniform weighting (Briggs weighting with robust=0.5 as defined by casa) was used to image the masers

continuum_subtraction.value: Continuum subtracted from each data set using line-free channels

evidence.quote: The continuum was subtracted from each data set
All image extents were $\le$80% of the primary beam, so no primary beam correction was applied.

smoothing.value: No spectral averaging; Hanning smoothing in correlator

evidence.quote: No spectral averaging was applied

what.value: Centre of expansion estimation by maximising maser separation near V*

evidence.loc: VY CMa continuum and maser morphology
evidence.quote: We estimated the centre of expansion of each line as in (cite: Richards12), by maximising the separation between masers at close to $V_{\star}$
We grouped the maser components into features comprising series of components in successive channels within the position errors, as in Richards et al. (2012)

method.value: Standard ALMA calibration with Pallas flux scale, J0522-3627 bandpass, J0648-3044 phase reference; self-cal on brightest maser channel

evidence.quote: The bright QSO J0522-3627 was used for bandpass calibration.

validation.value: Channel-to-channel position scatter and flux spectral index ~2 checked

evidence.quote: the flux density was consistent with the expected spectral index $\sim$2

method.value: Natural-weighted continuum; continuum-subtracted maser cubes with robust=0.5

evidence.quote: The continuum channels were imaged using natural weighting

method.value: 2D Gaussian fits per channel; components >3σ (321, 325) or >4σ (658), at least three successive channels

evidence.quote: We rejected components that did not form series of at least three in successive channels, within the maximum position uncertainty.
The relative position uncertainties are given by (beam size)/S/N

validation.value: Sidelobe components rejected; cross-match compared with 50 mas shifted data

evidence.quote: applying a 50 mas shift to one data set produces a similar number of pairs, so this seems like random coincidence.

method.value: Collisional excitation, radiative decay, escape-probability trapping with steep velocity gradient; negative optical depth contours vs T and n(H2)

evidence.quote: We treated the effects of radiative trapping with the use of an escape probability method and the assumption of a steep velocity gradient in a single direction
These optical depths were computed in the unsaturated limit
Normal ALMA calibration and imaging procedures were followed, using casa (http://casa.nrao.edu).

evidence.quote: We measured the positions of the masers and continuum peaks by fitting Gaussian components using the aips task sad

findings_qualitative.value: VY coincides with maser centre of expansion and is the stellar position

evidence.quote: **VY** coincides with the maser centre of expansion and is almost certainly the location of the star.

claims.hypothesis: Sub-mm H2O masers lie at increasing distances from the star in order 658, 321, 325 GHz
claims.experiment: Gaussian fitting of maser components in ALMA SV cubes
claims.result: Inner rims at successively larger distances; outer rims ~200, 500, 600 mas
claims.finding: Maser shells are distinct but overlapping, as predicted but reaching unexpectedly large radii

evidence.quote: The 658, 321, and 325 GHz masers lie in irregular, thick shells at increasing distances from the centre of expansion.

claims.hypothesis: The star is at the centre of expansion
claims.experiment: Compare maser expansion centre with continuum peaks
claims.result: Centre lies at compact peak VY, NW of brightest continuum C

evidence.quote: For the first time this is confirmed as the stellar position, coinciding with a compact peak offset to the NW of the brightest continuum emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Experimental SV observations with phase ambiguities and atmospheric phase errors; single epoch

evidence.quote: some observational methods were experimental, for example the duration of phase-referencing cycles turned out to allow a few phase ambiguities at the highest frequencies.

referee_caveats_inferred: Absolute astrometry uncertain (35 mas) so VY identification relies on phase transfer
Excitation model is simple and 658 GHz not shown
